# Every way an EraInfra Profile is deliberately not `ubuntu-latest`.
#
# `diff.sh` fingerprints a job on `ubuntu-latest` and on each Linux Profile and
# fails on every difference this file does not account for. So this file is the
# written record of the decisions: what we chose to be different about, and why.
# It did not exist before #82, which is why #80 -- a job capped at 8 CPUs while
# every interface it could read said 64 -- reached a production repository and
# was found by a user's test suite.
#
# Three directives, each of which MUST carry a `# reason`. An entry with no
# reason is a bug being hidden, so diff.sh treats a missing reason as a syntax
# error rather than a style preference.
#
#   allow <key-or-glob>            a difference in this key is intended
#   require <key>=<value>          this key must hold this value on EVERY leg
#   never-allow <key-or-glob>      `allow` may never name this key
#   pending <key>=<value> <date>   seen, owned by an issue, and time-boxed
#
# The differ warns about `allow` entries that matched no difference in a run.
# Most of those are rot and should go. A few are not: `runner_version` and
# `runner_action_archive_cache` are traceable to decisions here and merely
# happen to agree with GitHub's image this week, so they stay and the warning is
# expected. "Settled" means the reason no longer holds, not that the values
# matched once.
#
# `allow` and `pending` are different claims and the difference is the point.
# `allow` says "we meant this"; it is permanent and it requires the difference
# to be traceable to a decision recorded in this repository -- a flag in a
# provisioner, a line in the Dockerfile, an ADR, a documented product
# statement. `pending` says "we measured this, an issue owns it, and this line
# dies on that date". It pins the measured value, so a divergence that gets
# WORSE still fails, and it expires, so a question cannot be answered by
# forgetting it. Writing `allow` for something nobody has decided is the single
# way this file could become worse than useless.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The two keys that are not negotiable
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# #80 is not "the CPU count differs". Of course it differs: a Worker is a
# different size from a hosted runner, and the entries further down say so. #80
# is that the count a job SEES disagreed with the count it was ALLOWED -- 64
# against a quota of 8 -- so every tool that autosizes (vitest, `make -j`,
# Go, the JVM, Python) oversubscribed by 8x. That gap is what the
# `*_matches_allowed` keys measure, and there is no fleet anywhere on which it
# is intended.
#
# They are handled twice on purpose:
#
#   `never-allow` stops the plausible entry. Someone reading a red job at 03:00
#   will reach for "our machines are bigger, allow it"; that reasoning is
#   correct for `cpu_visible_count` and fatal for this key, so the attempt is a
#   hard failure instead of a comment nobody reads.
#
#   `require` stops the silent one. This job is differential, and a
#   differential job cannot see a defect that both legs share: if hosted and
#   Profile were both misreporting their own size the two values would agree
#   and the diff would go green. These are asserted absolutely, per leg.
require cpu_visible_matches_allowed=yes  # a machine that reports more CPUs than its own quota allows lies to every build tool that autosizes; this is #80
require mem_visible_matches_allowed=yes  # `free` and os.totalmem() read /proc/meminfo, which is the host's unless LXCFS is mounted, so a job can be OOM-killed at its cgroup limit while believing it has the host's RAM; this is the second half of #80
never-allow cpu_visible_matches_allowed  # the excusable difference is cpu_visible_nproc, which is allowed below; the agreement between what a job sees and what it may use is not
never-allow mem_visible_matches_allowed  # same shape as the CPU key: sizes may differ between legs, a machine disagreeing with itself may not
never-allow node_heap_within_allowed_mem  # Node sizes its default old space from total RAM, so a heap ceiling above the cgroup limit entitles a process to grow until the kernel kills it, and the OOM carries no stack

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The boundary itself
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
allow kernel_release  # a GitHub-hosted job runs on Azure's kernel; a Profile runs on the Worker's, or on the guest kernel deploy/provision-firecracker-host.sh pins. Both are pinned deliberately and neither tracks the other
allow virtualisation  # hosted is an Azure VM; the transitional Docker executor is a container and Firecracker is a microVM (ADR 0001)
allow container_hint  # the Docker executor is a container by construction, and says so; it is the trusted-repository fallback until #17 cuts over
allow cgroup_version  # the executor inherits the Worker host's cgroup hierarchy, and our hosts are not all on the same one; the numbers underneath it are read for v1 and v2 alike
allow seccomp_mode  # the Docker executor runs under Docker's default seccomp profile; a hosted VM job runs unfiltered
allow lsm_profile  # same reason: Docker applies its default AppArmor profile to the container
allow dev_kvm  # GitHub enabled nested virtualisation on hosted Linux runners; the shared-kernel Docker executor exposes no device nodes at all, which #80's own evidence records as kvm=absent. Firecracker guests get real vCPUs instead (#17)
allow dev_fuse  # measured absent on the fleet, and the same decision as dev_kvm above: provision-docker.sh passes no --device and no --cap-add, and the daily smoke canary fails if a host mount ever appears
allow dev_net_tun  # same: no device node reaches an Attempt, which is what a shared-kernel boundary buys
allow dev_vhost_vsock  # same
allow dev_loop_control  # same; a job that needs to mount an image needs the Firecracker executor (#17)
allow dev_dri  # same; no GPU is exposed to any Profile today

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Size. A Profile is a contract for a size, and it is not ubuntu-latest's
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each of these differs because a Profile carries `vcpus` and `memoryMiB`
# (convex/schema.ts) and a hosted runner carries whatever GitHub sells. None of
# them can express #80 on its own, which is exactly why the derived keys above
# exist and are not on this list.
allow cpu_visible_nproc  # a Profile's vcpus is not ubuntu-latest's 4
allow cpu_nproc_all  # the Worker host's core count, which no Profile promises to match
allow cpu_cpuinfo_count  # the Worker host's processor list, which /proc/cpuinfo reports whole and which no cpuset can narrow. The count differing between legs is a size difference; whether it agrees with nproc is a separate key and is not on this list
allow cpu_affinity_count  # the scheduler affinity mask a Profile hands the job
allow cpu_online_count  # the Worker host's online CPU set
allow cpu_cgroup_cpuset_count  # the cpuset width the executor allocates per Attempt
allow cpu_cgroup_quota_millicpu  # the CFS bandwidth quota, which is the Profile's vcpus on our side and unset on a hosted VM
allow cpu_allowed_millicpu  # the resolved ceiling of the two above
allow cpu_node_available_parallelism  # what Node reports, which follows the affinity mask
allow mem_visible_mib  # the Worker host's RAM, which no Profile promises to match
allow mem_allowed_mib  # the Profile's memoryMiB against whatever the hosted runner ships
allow mem_cgroup_limit_mib  # the executor sets a memory ceiling per Attempt; a hosted VM has none
allow mem_node_totalmem_mib  # the same host RAM read through os.totalmem()
allow mem_swap_total_mib  # swap is a property of the Worker host, not of the Profile
allow node_heap_limit_mib  # V8 sizes its default old space from total RAM, so this moves with the number above it; whether it FITS is the assertion, and it is not on this list
allow pids_cgroup_max  # apps/action-runner-agent/provisioners/provision-docker.sh sets --pids-limit 4096 as a deliberate blast-radius bound

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
allow workspace_fstype  # the Docker executor's writable layer is overlayfs and is destroyed with the Attempt; a hosted runner writes to the VM's own filesystem
allow scratch_fstype  # same layer
allow root_fstype  # same layer
# The three *_free_gib_pow2 keys had entries here until the first fleet run
# measured both legs into the same 64 GiB bucket. Nothing in this repository
# decides how much disk a Worker has, so an entry for it was speculation, and a
# speculative entry that matches nothing is exactly the rot this file cannot
# afford. If the buckets ever diverge the job goes red and somebody writes a
# real line with a measured reason, which is the outcome that was wanted.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The runner and its image
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
allow runner_environment  # `self-hosted` against `github-hosted` is the entire premise of the comparison
allow runner_version  # GitHub updates the hosted runner continuously; images/ubuntu-24.04-js/Dockerfile pins actions/runner by version and SHA-256, and that pin is asserted there
allow runner_image_os  # ImageOS is set by GitHub's image provisioning and by nothing of ours
allow runner_action_archive_cache  # provision-docker.sh points the runner at the image's read-only /opt/action-cache so a job does not fetch its Actions over the network
allow env_path  # the runner root and tool cache live at different paths in the two images. Whether a workflow can still FIND its tools is asserted by the tool_*_present keys, which are not on this list
allow user_groups  # the Image Release creates the runner account with exactly the docker and sudo groups; GitHub's image adds a dozen more for tooling we deliberately do not ship
allow user_gid  # images/ubuntu-24.04-js/Dockerfile creates the runner account with `useradd --gid docker`, so its primary group is docker rather than a same-named user group. That is what lets a job reach the Docker group without a second membership lookup
allow toolcache_tools  # the Image Release is minimal on purpose (docs/research/blacksmith-runner-images.md): it carries the toolchain its Profiles were built for and is not advertised as GitHub-hosted-compatible
allow toolcache_node_versions  # same: one pinned Node, seeded so actions/setup-node resolves it without a download
allow tool_*_version  # our Image Release pins its toolchain and GitHub's floats, so version drift between the two is expected. A tool DISAPPEARING is not, and tool_*_present is not on this list -- that is the #48 bug class
allow docker_daemon_reachable  # no Docker control socket is mounted into an Attempt, and the daily smoke canary fails if one ever is. A workflow that needs `docker build` cannot have it on this executor, and that is a decision rather than an accident
allow docker_server_version  # follows from the line above
allow tool_pnpm_present  # the Image Release installs pnpm 11.21.0 (images/ubuntu-24.04-js/Dockerfile) and GitHub's does not ship it at all, measured. A tool we have and they do not cannot break a workflow written for ubuntu-latest; the reverse can, which is why the rest of tool_*_present is not on this list

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deliberately NOT allowlisted, though it will fail
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cpu_nproc_matches_cpuinfo. Not today: both numbers are the host's 64 and they
# agree, so this key is `yes` on both legs and says nothing. It exists for the
# day #80's cpuset allocator lands. Measured on a production Worker (cgroup v1,
# Docker 28.1.1): a container run with `--cpus 8 --cpuset-cpus 0-7` reports
# nproc=8 and still lists 64 processors in /proc/cpuinfo. So the fix moves the
# defect rather than removing it -- cpu_visible_matches_allowed goes green and
# THIS key goes red -- and the entry that belongs here on that day is roughly:
#
#   allow cpu_nproc_matches_cpuinfo  # known residue of #80's cpuset fix: nproc
#   and the quota agree, /proc/cpuinfo still reports the host, so anything
#   parsing it directly is still told the wrong number
#
# It is written here as prose rather than as an entry precisely because it has
# not happened yet. Allowlisting a difference nobody has measured is how a
# record becomes a wish.
#
# dev_shm_size_mib. `ubuntu-latest` measures 7995 MiB, half its RAM; the fleet
# measures 64 MiB and stays at 64 MiB whatever --memory says, because
# --shm-size is never passed and Docker's default is a fixed 64 MB. That was
# the first thing this job found that nobody had written down, it is #80's
# shape exactly -- a resource a job is silently much smaller in than every
# interface it can read suggests -- and it is filed as #87. It has a `pending`
# entry below and it will never get an `allow` one: nothing here chose 64 MiB,
# and an `allow` line would convert an unowned Docker default into a decision
# this repository never made, which is the precise mistake this file exists to
# stop.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deliberately not fingerprinted
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recorded here because "why is X not checked" is the second question anyone
# asks this file, and because a dimension dropped without a note reads later
# like a dimension nobody thought of.
#
#   hostname, container id, IP addresses, uptime, PIDs, timestamps -- they move
#   between two runs on the SAME machine, so they cannot be diffed between two
#   different ones. Free space is fingerprinted as a power-of-two bucket for
#   the same reason.
#
#   CPU model, vendor and instruction-set flags -- GitHub rotates hosted
#   hardware, so these differ from ubuntu-latest to ubuntu-latest. A dimension
#   that is not stable on the baseline cannot be conformance-checked against
#   it; a build that needs AVX-512 needs a Profile that promises it, which is a
#   Profile contract question and not this job's.
#
#   ImageVersion -- GitHub bumps it weekly. It would be an allowlisted key that
#   never fails, i.e. noise. The workflow prints it in the run summary instead.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recorded, owned, and time-boxed — NOT intended
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `pending` is not an allowlist entry. It says: this difference was measured,
# an issue owns it, and this line dies on that date. It fails if the divergence
# gets worse than the value recorded here, and it fails outright once the date
# passes, so it cannot quietly become permanent the way an `allow` with a
# hand-wave reason can. Everything below arrived in the FIRST run against a real
# Worker (run 32092987570): 103 keys identical, 45 differences already accounted
# for above, and these 34 that nobody had written down.
#
# The rule that decides which list a difference lands on: `allow` requires the
# difference to be traceable to a decision recorded in this repository — a flag
# in a provisioner, a line in the Dockerfile, an ADR, a documented product
# statement. Everything else is `pending` with an issue, because "nobody has
# looked at this yet" and "we meant this" are different claims and only one of
# them belongs in an allowlist.

# #80, live on the deployed fleet. nproc reports 64 against a 2-CPU quota and
# /proc/meminfo reports 251 GiB against a 2 GiB limit — a factor of 125. #83 is
# MERGED but the Worker still runs a provisioner that predates it, so this is
# deployment lag rather than a new defect, and this job will keep saying so
# until the rollout reaches the fleet. These two keys are `never-allow`
# precisely so nobody can retire them by calling them intended; recording that
# they are currently true is the opposite of that, and is what these lines do.
pending cpu_visible_matches_allowed=no 2026-11-16  # #80 measured live on the fleet: cpu_visible_nproc=64 against cpu_cgroup_quota_millicpu=2000. Fix #83 is merged; delete this line when the rollout reaches the Workers
pending mem_visible_matches_allowed=no 2026-11-16  # the other half of #80, which #83 explicitly does not fix: mem_visible_mib=257581 against mem_cgroup_limit_mib=2048. Needs LXCFS or the limit exported into the job

# #87, now confirmed on real hardware rather than inferred from Docker's
# documented default.
pending dev_shm_size_mib=64 2026-11-16  # #87: provision-docker.sh never passes --shm-size, so every Attempt gets Docker default 64 MiB against 7995 on hosted, whatever the Profile memoryMiB says

# #92 — the 31 the first fleet run turned up that nobody has decided about.
# Each needs one of two answers before the date: fix it, or promote it to an
# `allow` line with the reason it is intended. Re-dating is not an answer.
pending tool_ssh_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending tool_python3_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending tool_zstd_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending tool_gh_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending tool_go_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending tool_pip3_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending tool_rsync_present=no 2026-11-16  # #92: present on ubuntu-latest, absent from the Image Release — the #48 bug class on Linux
pending locale_lang=unset 2026-11-16  # #92: unset here against C.UTF-8 on hosted, so the C library falls back to ASCII and any date, sort or non-ASCII assertion can pass there and fail here
pending locale_charmap=ANSI_X3.4-1968 2026-11-16  # #92: the consequence of the line above, measured
pending locale_has_en_us_utf8=no 2026-11-16  # #92: no en_US.UTF-8 locale is generated in the Image Release
pending tz_name=unavailable 2026-11-16  # #92: neither /etc/timezone nor /etc/localtime exists, so the container is UTC by absence and a named zone lookup errors rather than resolving
pending sysctl_vm_max_map_count=65530 2026-11-16  # #92: the Worker host runs kernel 5.4 with the old default against 262144 on hosted; Elasticsearch and OpenSearch refuse to start below 262144
pending sysctl_fs_inotify_max_user_instances=128 2026-11-16  # #92: the Worker host kernel setting, which nothing in this repository chose
pending sysctl_fs_inotify_max_user_watches=524288 2026-11-16  # #92: the Worker host kernel setting, which nothing in this repository chose
pending sysctl_kernel_threads_max=2059180 2026-11-16  # #92: the Worker host kernel setting, which nothing in this repository chose
pending sysctl_user_max_user_namespaces=1029590 2026-11-16  # #92: the Worker host kernel setting, which nothing in this repository chose
pending sysctl_vm_swappiness=100 2026-11-16  # #92: the Worker host kernel setting, which nothing in this repository chose
pending rlimit_max_locked_memory_soft=65536 2026-11-16  # #92: 64 KiB against 8 MiB on hosted; anything that mlocks key material notices
pending rlimit_max_locked_memory_hard=65536 2026-11-16  # #92: as above, hard limit
pending rlimit_max_open_files_soft=1048576 2026-11-16  # #92: LARGER than hosted, which is not automatically better — code that walks the fd range on fork stalls measurably at a million
pending rlimit_max_open_files_hard=1048576 2026-11-16  # #92: as above, hard limit
pending rlimit_max_processes_soft=unlimited 2026-11-16  # #92: unlimited here against 63838 on hosted, so a blast-radius bound hosted has is absent here
pending rlimit_max_processes_hard=unlimited 2026-11-16  # #92: as above, hard limit
pending rlimit_max_core_file_size_soft=unlimited 2026-11-16  # #92: a Docker daemon default nothing in this repository chose, same gap as #87
pending rlimit_max_pending_signals_soft=1029590 2026-11-16  # #92: a Docker daemon default nothing in this repository chose, same gap as #87
pending rlimit_max_pending_signals_hard=1029590 2026-11-16  # #92: a Docker daemon default nothing in this repository chose, same gap as #87
pending rlimit_max_stack_size_soft=8388608 2026-11-16  # #92: a Docker daemon default nothing in this repository chose, same gap as #87
pending dns_nameserver_count=2 2026-11-16  # #92: the resolver shape a container inherits rather than one anyone picked. All four dns_resolves_* probes are identical and green on both legs; short-name resolution and retry behaviour are what differ
